open_obligations: Note that Michael et al.'s GPT-4 consultants were poor at arguing wrong answers, unlike Khan et al.'s optimised GPT-4-Turbo.
Check the size of Khan et al.'s incorrect-consultant accuracy drop.
Check that judge interaction is allowed in both consultancy setups.
in.other_title: Judge interaction does not raise human debate accuracy; incorrect consultants mislead
in.rationale: Michael et al. report dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time on QuALITY-hard. Khan et al. report that in consultancy incorrect experts cause low human judge accuracy, suggesting it is easier to be misled in consultancy; Khan et al.'s consultants are GPT-4-Turbo, whereas Michael et al. found dishonest GPT-4 consultants did not mislead judges much (87% accuracy), so the support is for strong consultants.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether dishonest consultants mislead human judges in hidden-passage QuALITY consultancy

text: Splitting consultancies by consultant honesty, the paper reports that dishonest human consultants successfully deceive judges 40% of the time, while for GPT-4 consultants judges do better when the consultant is dishonest (87% accuracy) than when honest (74%). The authors attribute higher AI-consultancy accuracy at least in part to the AI being much worse at arguing convincingly for the wrong answer.
title: Dishonest human consultants deceive judges 40% of the time; dishonest GPT-4 ones do not
